correctness.rationale: Translate each surviving-dependent-species event to absence of an edge in the deleted vertex set, hence R_t(G)=1−i_t(G)/binom(n,t) exactly; independent patch losses have no-extinction probability (1−q)^n I_G(q/(1−q)). For every component C_l use transfer roots u+v=1, uv=−z, so I_Ca I_Cb−I_C(a+b)=(−z)^min(a,b)L_|a−b|(z). Every proposed split and exceptional finite rewrite has coefficientwise correct sign; repeated 3-splits decrease to residue-correct C3/C4/C5, repeated 4-splits increase to C4/C5/C6/C7. Strict polynomial inequality for z>0 establishes uniqueness by isomorphism, not necessarily at a single t. Independent exact-integer enumeration of all 1,554 2-regular cycle partitions n=3..29 reproduced both bounds and uniqueness, and the nine-patch i3 values 27 versus 30. The symbolic transformation argument supplies all n, not finite census.
residual_risks: Finite independent computations and package checkers are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge: Zhao's regular-graph independence polynomial bound proves a stronger pointwise all-graph upper bound in the order-divisible-by-four subcase; it does not imply coefficientwise domination at every size t or identify the optimal residual cycles for all n. Alexander–Mink addresses fixed small k; related ecological records analyze moments or general network dependence, not the full all-deletion-count extremal polynomial. The graph polynomial itself is classical, and a complete uncatalogued 2-regular coefficientwise extremal theorem would be decisive if located; no such theorem was identified in material inspected.
residual_risks: Known sharp pointwise upper bound already covers C4 optimizer for n≡0 (mod4) under iid-loss activity; this subcase alone is not novel.
